newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Petroleum drives BHP Q3 profit hike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Petroleum drives BHP Q3 profit hike.

text.p: A doubling of profits from the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) Petroleum division was a key driver in the 69.5 percent rise in the resources giant's third quarter profit to A$378 million.

BHP said higher oil and gas prices, along with favourable tax adjustments, helped boost the petroleum division's profit to A$246 million for the three months to February 28, up from A$121 million in the same quarter a year earlier.
BHP earlier reported its overall group sales rose 11.8 percent to A$5.144 billion and set a steady final dividend of 26 cents.
Earnings per share rose to 22.9 cents from 13.8 cents.
BHP Copper's profits rose to A$145 million from A$88 million, due to higher output, better prices and lower costs.

"Major factors affecting sales revenues were: inclusion of revenues from the North American copper and Tubemakers operations which were acquired in January and April 1996 respectively, higher U.S. dollar prices for iron ore, coal, copper, oil and gas and higher shipments of iron ore, coal, oil and copper," BHP said.
"These were partly offset by lower natural gas volumes, lower steel export prices and the adverse impact of the higher A$/US$ exchange rate," it said.
BHP said the February 1996 quarter was depressed due mainly to lower Copper and Steel results.
Third quarter profits from its steel division rose to A$72 million from A$44 million a year ago, due to lower costs from a better manufacturing performance and lower employee numbers.
The inclusion of Tubemaker results helped the steel result, but this was partly offset by lower export prices.

BHP said higher prices for its petroleum products was a major factor in the stronger profits from the division. It said its averaged realised oil price for the quarter was A$31.36 a barrel, up from A$26.30 in the same quarter a year earlier.
"Realised oil prices peaked in January and have since declined," BHP said.
Petroleum's tax expense fell because of certain tax effects from overseas exploration and a cut in prior period tax provision.

"There was also a net profit of A$16 million from the sale of Gulf of Mexico assets and an Australian exploration permit," it said. Gas volumes fell because of the sale of some U.S. and offshore Netherlands assets.
Group tax rose A$31 million to A$229 million, representing a tax rate of 34.2 percent, down from 43.4 percent in 1996.
This was lower than the 36 percent nominal Australian corporate tax rate, due to the recognition of a tax benefit now available on some exploration expenditure because of the Magma acquisition.
This was partly offset by an under-provision of tax on prior year's interest receipts.
The third quarter profit of A$378 million compared with analysts' expectations of A$330 million to A$370 million.
By 1.10 p.m. (0210 GMT), BHP shares were two cents lower at A$17.11 after trading as high as A$17.32 before the result and off a low of A$17.05 after the result.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
